name: alphaNLI
description: Abductive Natural Language Inference (alphaNLI) is a benchmark for abductive commonsense reasoning. Given two observations (beginning and ending of a story), models choose the most plausible hypothesis that explains the transition between them from two options. Tests the ability to perform abductive inference in everyday situations.
reputation: Introduced abductive NLI task type; published at ICLR 2020; human performance ~91.4%; influential in reasoning research
notes: Introduced at ICLR 2020 (published as 'Abductive Commonsense Reasoning'). Training set: 169,654 examples; dev: 1,532; test: 3,059. Given observations O1 (beginning) and O2 (ending), models select the more plausible hypothesis H1 or H2. Inspired by Peirce's abductive reasoning. Contrasts with SNLI (deductive) and NLI (not explicitly abductive).
